limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

analysis.summary: In this round, 23 of 32 members chose the 328 HKD member fare, generating 7,544 HKD in base ticket receipts; no regular-fare purchases occurred. Nine members declined, all citing that no offered ticket was both available and within their basic-fare budget. Buyers described the member fare as a compelling bargain, often noting the 410 HKD normal fare as an acceptable fallback. These are stated intentions, not fulfilled purchases, and reasons are explanations rather than measured willingness to pay. Capacity was not binding and no inventory denials occurred.
analysis.hypothesis: Among members who decline at 328 HKD citing budget or availability, offering a lower member fare would raise stated purchase intention more than offering the 410 HKD normal fare, testable by comparing conversion across randomized price arms.
